Definition: Assir, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Assir is the name of two Israelites: a son of Korah, named in the genealogy of Levi, and a son of Jeconiah, named in the line of David after the exile — 'the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son.' One sits in the priestly line, the other in the royal line after the captivity.
TheologicalSignificance: Two men, one name, and both sit in the lines that matter most — Levi and David, priest and king, before and after the exile. I believe the name Assir is a quiet sign that God keeps both lines alive through the captivity: the priesthood and the promise survive together.
